NONE: › to make something more real or consider it as real
使物體化；使具體化

example: These phenomena are reified into facts.
這些現象被具體化後為事實。

NONE: C2 to be the king or queen of a country
為王，為君；當政；統治
C2 to be the main feeling or quality in a situation or person
主宰；起支配作用；盛行
C1 the period of time when a king or queen rules a country
為王，為君；當政；統治
› a period when a particular person, feeling, or quality is very important or has a strong influence
主宰（或支配）的時期

example: The bomb attacks produced a panic which reigned over the city.
炸彈襲擊引起的恐慌籠罩全城。
Love reigned supreme in her heart.
愛情完全佔據了她的心。
the reign of Henry VIII
亨利八世的統治
his successful reign as manager of the team
他以經理身份對這個小組的成功駕馭

NONE: › being the most recent winner of a competition
（體育競賽項目冠軍）本屆的

example: She's the reigning champion at Wimbledon.
她是本屆溫布頓網球賽冠軍。

NONE: › to make something such as a disagreement or worry that was disappearing grow stronger
重新激起

example: The recent food-poisoning scare has reignited debate/concern/controversy over farming methods.
最近的食物中毒恐慌會再次激起了人們對耕作方法的辯論／關注／爭論。
There are fears that rising wages will reignite inflation.
有人擔心工資上漲會再次引起通貨膨脹。

NONE: › a treatment that involves directing energy from your hands into someone's body to make them feel better
靈氣療法（一種治療方法，將你的能量透過手導入某人身體，使其感覺好一些）
› to pay back money to someone who has spent it for you or lost it because of you
償還；付還；補償

example: The airline reimbursed me for the amount they had overcharged me.
航空公司把多收的錢退還給我了。
She was reimbursed by the gas company for the damage to her house.
煤氣公司對她房屋遭受的損失進行了賠償。

NONE: › a long, thin piece of material, especially leather, that helps you to control and direct a horse
（尤指皮質的）繮繩
› UK a strap that is put around a small child's body or wrist and held at the other end by an adult so that the adult can stop the child running away
（領幼兒走路時防止其走失的）安全繩套，保護帶

example: You pull on both reins to stop or slow a horse, but only the left rein to turn left.
拉兩邊的繮繩來讓馬停住或放慢速度，但是要想左轉時，只需拉左邊的繮繩。
I always put my son on reins when we go shopping.
我們帶兒子去購物時，總是用安全帶牽著他。

NONE: › to make a horse go more slowly or stop by pulling on its reins
用繮繩勒住（馬）；收繮繩使（馬）放慢速度（或停住）
› also rein sth back to control an emotion, activity, or situation to prevent it from becoming too powerful
抑制；控制；約束

example: We tried to rein in our excitement and curiosity.
我們盡力克制住興奮和好奇。
Reports today suggest consumers are already reining back spending.
今天發表的調查報告顯示，消費者已經開始控制花銷。

T always passive: › [ T always passive ] If a dead person or animal is reincarnated as someone or something else, their spirit returns to life in that person or animal.
T: › [ T ] If something is reincarnated, it appears in a different form, especially after it has disappeared for a period of time.
再生；（尤指消失一段時間後）以不同的形式出現

example: Compared to the old model, the reincarnated Mini Cooper has a more powerful engine and looks more streamlined.
與其舊型號比較，新款迷你車的引擎動力更強，線條也更圓潤。

U: › [ U ] the belief that a dead person's spirit returns to life in another body
C: › [ C ] a person or animal in whose body a dead person's spirit returns to life

example: Hindus and Buddhists believe in reincarnation.
印度教徒和佛教徒相信輪回轉世說。
He believes he's a reincarnation of Julius Caesar.
他認爲自己是尤利烏斯．凱撒再生。

NONE: › a type of deer with large horns that lives in the northern parts of Europe, Asia, and North America
馴鹿

example: Santa Claus travels in a sleigh pulled by reindeer.
聖誕老人乘坐馴鹿拉的雪橇出行。

NONE: C2 to make something stronger
加固；使更結實
C1 If something reinforces an idea or opinion, it provides more proof or support for it and makes it seem true.
強化，加深，進一步證實（觀點、看法等）
› to provide an army with more soldiers or weapons to make it stronger
增援；加強…的力量；給…增強裝備

example: The pockets on my jeans are reinforced with double stitching.
我牛仔褲的口袋縫了兩道線，很結實。
The final technical report into the accident reinforces the findings of initial investigations.
對事故作出的最終的技術性報告進一步證實了最初的調查結果。
His behaviour merely reinforced my dislike of him.
他的行為只能使我更討厭他。
The garrison is to be reinforced with/by another two battalions of soldiers.
守備部隊將得到另外兩個營的增援。

NONE: › concrete that contains metal rods to make it stronger
鋼筋混凝土

U: › [ U ] the act of making something stronger
› soldiers sent to join an army to make it stronger

example: The harbour walls need urgent reinforcement.
海港堤垻急需加固。

NONE: › to give someone back their previous job or position, or to cause something to exist again
使重返崗位，使恢復原職；把…放回原處；使恢復原狀

example: A month after being unfairly dismissed, he was reinstated in his job.
在被不公正解職一個月後，他又重新返回工作崗位。

NONE: › the act of giving someone back their job or making something exist again
重返崗位，恢復原職；復原

example: The union demanded the immediate reinstatement of all the workers who'd been sacked.
工會要求立即讓所有被解僱的工人重返崗位。
Reinstatement of the tax would be a disaster.
恢復該項稅收將是一場災難。

NONE: › to produce something new that is based on something that already exists
（在已有事物的基礎上）重新創造，改造
› to change your job and/or the way you look and behave so that you seem very different
（透過改換工作或形象、行為方式而）改造自己，洗心革面，換個活法

example: The story of Romeo and Juliet was reinvented as a Los Angeles gangster movie.
羅密歐和朱麗葉的故事被改編成了一部洛杉磯黑幫題材電影。
He's one of those sportsmen who reinvent themselves as TV presenters.
他是那些半路出家做電視節目主持人的運動員之一。

NONE: › to waste time trying to create something that someone else has already created
重複發明；無謂地重複；浪費時間做無用功

T: › to make someone feel healthier, and more energetic again
使恢復健康，使恢復元氣
› to make something stronger, or more exciting or successful again
給恢復強大；使更為興奮（或成功）

example: His beliefs, both political and religious, seem to reinvigorate him.
他的政治和宗教信仰似乎讓他恢復了活力。
Lower interest rates could reinvigorate consumer spending and the struggling housing market.
更低的利率可能會重振消費和疲軟的住房市場。

NONE: › to print or produce something again
重印；重新發行；再版

example: The recording has been reissued to celebrate the conductor's 80th birthday.
為了慶祝這位指揮家的80壽辰，重新發行了這張唱片。

NONE: › to say something again, once or several times
反復地說，反復講；重申

example: The government has reiterated its refusal to compromise with terrorists.
政府重申拒絕向恐怖分子妥協。
[ + that ] She reiterated that she had never seen him before.
她一再重申自己以前從未見過他。
